newsitem.title: FINLAND: LANOR CUTS STAKE IN ASKO TO 11 PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: LANOR CUTS STAKE IN ASKO TO 11 PERCENT.

text.p: Finnish plastics pipe and furniture group Asko Oy said in a statement on Wednesday holding company Lanor had cut its stake in it to 11 percent from 23 percent at the turn of the year.
"During the spring, Lanor has been selling Asko shares so that the holding at the turn of the year (23 percent) has fallen to about 11 percent currently," Asko said.
It said Lanor was unwinding itself with the aim to "widen Asko's ownership base and improve the liquidity of the stock."
The remaining Asko shares would be distributed to Lanor's owners in proportion to their holdings in it.
Asko itself owns 47 percent of Lanor, oil and chemicals group Neste owns another 47 percent and insurer Sampo owns about six percent, Asko said.
"Asko and Neste will each get amounts that represent about five percent of Asko's shares and Sampo group about 0.6 percent," it said.
The new Finnish company act allows companies to hold five percent of their own stock.
